'''Gábor Hraskó''' (born 26 August 1963) is a Hungarian [[science communicator]] and [[scientific skepticism|skeptic]], well known within the Hungarian and international movement as the president of the [[Hungarian Skeptic Society]]<ref name="SzT">{{cite web|title=Members – Hungarian Skeptic Society|url=http://www.ecso.org/member-org/hungarian-skeptic-society|publisher=[[European Council of Skeptical Organisations]]|date=24 May 2014|accessdate=18 November 2015}}</ref> and chairman of the [[European Council of Skeptical Organisations]] (2013-2017).<ref name="ECSO">{{cite web|title=ECSO profile – Skeptics in Europe|url=http://www.ecso.org/about-us|date=7 February 2008|accessdate=18 November 2015}}</ref> He is a member of the Club of Hungarian Science Journalists,<ref>{{cite web|title=Members of TÚK (Club of Hungarian Science Journalists)|date=19 June 2023 |url=http://tuk.hu/nevsor.html|language=Hungarian}}</ref> author of the ''"X-Aknák"'' popular science blog, and was co-editor and co-host of the television series of the same name.<ref>{{cite web|title=Vágó Síkra száll az ezoterikusok ellen|url=http://index.hu/kultur/media/xaknak|publisher=index.hu|date=26 May 2003|accessdate=18 November 2015|language=Hungarian}}</ref> Hraskó is a scientific and technical consultant for the [[Committee for Skeptical Inquiry]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=Scientific and Technical Consultants|journal=Skeptical Inquirer|date=2016|volume=40|issue=2|page=67}}</ref>

==Personal life and education==
He's the oldest son of Péter Hraskó,<ref name="Family">{{cite web|url=http://www.hrasko.com|title=Home page of the Hraskó family|language=Hungarian}}</ref> renowned physicist, recognised for his research and teaching activities on the field of [[Theory of relativity|relativity]].<ref>{{cite book|first=Péter| last=Hraskó|title=Basic Relativity: An Introductory Essay|publisher=[[Springer Science+Business Media|Springer]]|isbn=978-3642178092|year=2011| id= {{ASIN|364217809X|country=uk}}}}</ref>

Following his high school graduation in 1981,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://oregdiak.ejg.hu/download/tablók/tablok1981/1981c.jpg|title=1981-es tabló – Eötvös József Gimnázium fizika-kémia tagozat|language=Hungarian}}</ref> he went on to study [[biology]] at the [[Eötvös Loránd University]], where he finished his studies with a Research master's degree in 1987. After that he worked as a biologist at the [[Zoology]] Department of the [[Hungarian Natural History Museum]] until 1989, when he moved on to the field of [[Information technology|IT]].

== Career as a skeptic ==

===Science educator===
[[File:Gábor Hraskó homeopathy talk.JPG|thumb|250px|Gábor Hraskó giving a talk on [[homeopathy]] at an event organised by the [[Hungarian Skeptic Society]] in 2012]]
His first science education writings were published in 1999 in the Hungarian journal Természet Világa,<ref>{{cite journal|first=Gábor|last=Hraskó|title=Teleportáció|journal=Természet Világa|url=http://www.hrasko.com/xaknak.php?docid=10002|volume=130|issue=7|pages=296–301|language=Hungarian|accessdate=18 November 2015}}</ref> in a special column that lasted 3 issues and was given the title Szkeptikus Sarok (translates as 'Skeptical Corner').<ref>{{cite web|title=Természet Világa – Szkeptikus Sarok|url=http://www.termeszetvilaga.hu/szkeptikus/index.html|language=Hungarian|accessdate=18 November 2015}}</ref> This was followed by several other articles, but in 2001 he started his own [[Scientific skepticism|skeptical]] blog with the title X-Aknák (translates to 'X-Mines', with reference to the then very popular series, the [[X-Files]]).

[[File:Gábor Hraskó at ESC2015.JPG|thumb|250px|Gábor Hraskó at the 16th [[European Skeptics Congress]] in London]]
In 2003 the same title was used for a TV series he co-edited and co-hosted with the Hungarian [[Game show|quiz show]] host and fellow skeptic [[István Vágó]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hraskó Gábor – X-Aknák az ATV-ben|url=http://www.hrasko.com/xaknak.php?docid=10035|language=Hungarian|accessdate=18 November 2015}}</ref> The show featured lively debates with proponents of [[pseudoscience|pseudoscientific]] claims and lasted only 11 episodes before it was shut down by the channel (ATV), claiming there had been violent reactions from debated pseudoscientists and negative feedback from viewers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hrasko.com/xaknak.php?docid=90013|title=Hraskó Gábor – Vége! X-Aknák az ATV-n|language=Hungarian|accessdate=18 November 2015}}</ref>

===Skeptical activist===
After the political changes in Hungary in 1990, many different claims of a pseudoscientific nature started to emerge in the country. To provide an organised force against pseudoscience, a group called ''Tényeket Tisztelők Társasága'' ("Society of the Respecters of Facts", also called 'Hungarian Skeptics') was brought to life in 1992.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.termeszetvilaga.hu/xaknak/10020/|title=A Tényeket Tisztelők Társasága alapszabálya|website=X-Aknák|publisher=Természet Világa|language=Hungarian|date=4 April 1997|accessdate=18 November 2015}}</ref> Although this was not an officially existing body, Gábor Hraskó became a board member and secretary, but after it became obvious that the purely academic style in the skeptic movement was not efficient, he and István Vágó started the preparations to establish an officially existing organisation to coordinate grassroots activism.<ref name="ESP">{{cite podcast|url=http://theesp.eu/podcast%20archive/episode_001_gabor_hrasko.html|title=Episode No. 001, feat. Gábor Hraskó|publisher=The [[European Skeptics Podcast]]|website=Theesp.eu|host=[[SoundCloud]]|date=3 May 2016|accessdate=3 May 2016}}</ref>

The future of scientific skepticism is improving, according to Hraskó, as popular movies are shifting away from scientists being the "bad guys" and more movies such as ''[[The Martian (film)|The Martian]]'', ''[[Interstellar (film)|Interstellar]]'' and ''[[Gravity (2013 film)|Gravity]]'' are making the heroes scientists. These movies are featuring good scientific content but still appeal to audiences not normally interested in science. This is a "great influence" and helping to change views on science. In order to facilitate a love of science, according to Hraskó, we need to tell good stories, "not to trap... but to explain... people are not rational animals... we have to teach them to become so". When asked what advice he would give someone interested in getting involved in the skeptical movement, he said, "You do not have to be a scientist or expert on a subject... you will learn as you go".<ref name="ESP"/>

{{Cquote|It's not just that we have to debunk things, we have to teach people how to think scientifically.<ref name="ESP"/> }}

===Role in the Hungarian skeptic movement===
In December 2006, the [[Hungarian Skeptic Society]] (HSS) was founded,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.szkeptikustarsasag.hu/news/97-hungarian-skeptic-society-was-founded|title=Hungarian Skeptic Society was founded|publisher=[[Hungarian Skeptic Society]]|date=16 December 2006|accessdate=19 November 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.szkeptikustarsasag.hu/dokumentumok/doc/3/raw|title=A Szkeptikus Társaság alapszabálya|language=Hungarian|date=21 June 2014|accessdate=19 November 2015}}</ref> with István Vágó elected president and Gábor Hraskó to become vice president of the organisation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.csicop.org/specialarticles/show/two_decades_of_skepticism_in_hungary_a_personal_view/|title=Two decades of skepticism in Hungary: A personal view|publisher=[[CSICOP]]|author=András G. Pintér|date=22 January 2015|accessdate=19 November 2015}}</ref> Then he went on to become COO in 2008 and president in 2009, a position he holds to date.

The Hungarian Skeptics originally began with the atheist movement, but they discovered that the two groups had different strategies, Hraskó explains that both are important, but the atheist group is more philosophical and has already reached the conclusion that God does not exist, no need to investigate. Whereas skeptics are more focused on the scientific method. As of the fall of 2015, there are 100 members of the Hungarian skeptic group.<ref name="ESP"/>

===Role in the European skeptic movement===
[[File:ECSO meeting 2015 London 2 (cropped).JPG|thumb|300px|left|The board of [[European Council of Skeptical Organisations|ECSO]] holding a meeting in London at the 16th European Skeptics Congress in 2015 (left to right): [[Tim Trachet]], [[Amardeo Sarma]], Michael Heap, Gábor Hraskó and [[Catherine de Jong]]]] 
After the HSS had joined the [[European Council of Skeptical Organisations]] (ECSO) in 2007,<ref>{{cite web|title=How the Hungarian Skeptic Society came to life|url=http://www.szkeptikustarsasag.hu/introduction|publisher=[[Hungarian Skeptic Society]]|accessdate=19 November 2015}}</ref> he acted as a chief organiser of the<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/skeptics.eu/posts/103121816417116|title=Thanks to Gabor Hrasko and the Hungarian skeptics…|author=ECSO – European Skeptics|publisher=Facebook|date=19 September 2010|accessdate=19 November 2015}}</ref> 14th [[European Skeptics Congress]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.szkeptikustarsasag.hu/14th-european-skeptic-congress|title=14th European Skeptics Congress|publisher=[[Hungarian Skeptic Society]]|date=11 August 2010|accessdate=19 November 2015}}</ref> held in Budapest in 2010, hosted by the Hungarian Skeptics.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://lanyrd.com/2010/european-skeptics/|title=14th European Skeptics Congress|publisher=Lanyrd|accessdate=19 November 2015}}</ref> He became vice chairman of the ECSO, then in 2013 he was elected chairman of the organisation at the 15th European Skeptics Congress in [[Stockholm]]. There he remained until the end of the 17th European Skeptics Congress, when he left the role and was replaced by Claire Klingenberg.<ref name=gerbicadventure>{{cite web|last1=Gerbic|first1=Susan|author-link=Susan Gerbic|title=Skeptical Adventures in Europe, Part 2|url=https://www.csicop.org/specialarticles/show/skeptical_adventures_in_europe_part_2|website=www.csicop.org|date=9 February 2018 |publisher=Committee for skeptical inquiry|accessdate=29 April 2018}}</ref>

In recent years, he has been attending skeptic meetings across Europe<ref>{{cite web|url=http://lanyrd.com/profile/ghrasko/|title=Gabor Hrasko's conference talks and presentations|publisher=[[Lanyrd]]|accessdate=19 November 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.worldskeptics.org/component/content/article/2-uncategorised/3-program|title=Program – 6th World Skeptics Congress|website=Worldskeptics.org|year=2012|accessdate=19 November 2015}}</ref> as well as still playing a leading role in the Hungarian movement at large.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.szkeptikustarsasag.hu/news/107-gabor-hrasko-on-cool-tv|title=Gábor Hraskó on Cool TV|publisher=[[Hungarian Skeptic Society]]|date=24 August 2007|accessdate=19 November 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=alFwjWet1G8|title=10:23 Homeopátia – Nincs benne semmi kampány túladagolási esemény (Budapest 2011/02/05 10:15–10:30)|publisher=YouTube|author=Hungarian Skeptic Society|author-link=Hungarian Skeptic Society|date=5 February 2011|accessdate=19 November 2015}}</ref>

When asked what the biggest challenges are for Hungary and Europe, Hraskó explained that when they started out in the early 1990s the focus was on UFOs and Astrology. Now the focus has changed to alt med and health scares, also more scientific centered topics like GMO's and global warming are becoming more important.<ref name="ESP"/>

=== Other appearances ===
At the 17th European Skeptics Congress, he chaired a panel on science and religion. Joining him on the panel were [[Konrad Talmont-Kamiński]], Gerald Ostdiek, Petr Jan Vinš, and [[Leo Igwe]].<ref name=gerbicadventure/>

== Public life ==
He was active in the international [[Green politics|green movement]] at the end of the 80s and beginning of the 90s and was a founding member of the [[Green Party of Hungary]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://feol.hu/hetvege/a-lenyeg-a-tudomany-1199105|title=A lényeg a tudomány|publisher=FMH Online|language=Hungarian|date=24 February 2007|accessdate=19 November 2015}}</ref> within which he was responsible for international relations from 1989. It was in this period, when he was chief organiser of the first Eastern European meeting of [[European Green Party|European Greens]] in Budapest in 1990.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=http://labourfocus.gn.apc.org/GreensLF61.html|title=The Greens in Eastern Europe|author=Gerhard Jordan|journal=Labour Focus on Eastern Europe|issue=61|year=1998|accessdate=19 November 2015}}</ref> He was also one of the leading members of the GreenWay movement as editor of their newsletter.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=Grünes Gedächtnis 2010|url=http://www.boell.de/sites/default/files/Jahrbuch_Gruenes_Gedaechtnis_2010.pdf|journal=Archiv Grünes Gedächtnis|language=German|year=2010|accessdate=19 November 2015}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Gábor Hraskó is an experienced [[hiking|hiker]] and an ardent [[Birdwatching|birdwatcher]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.birding.hu/useradatlap/3218|title=Adatlap|publisher=Birding.hu|language=Hungarian|accessdate=19 November 2015}}</ref> and also has a passion for flying, something he tries to satisfy with self-education through flight simulators.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://hu.linkedin.com/in/ghrasko|title=Gabor Hrasko – LinkedIn profile|publisher=[[LinkedIn]]|accessdate=19 November 2015}}</ref> Asked about his partaking in the [[10:23 Campaign]] in 2010, he said "I am a five-year survivor". Hraskó is married and has two daughters.<ref name="ESP"/>
